title: 3. Division, Berlin, 18 Nov 1933 → 3. (Preußische) Fahrabteilung, Berlin-Lankwitz: a Reichswehr exercise message ("Uebungsspruch") in five-letter groups
correspondents: 3. Division, Abt. Stonach (Berlin) → "Verteiler: Gruppe 3"; the copy received by the 3. (Preußische) Fahrabteilung, Berlin-Lankwitz
shelfmark: NARA RG 242, microfilm T405, roll 1 ("Number 1", NAID 332024052), frame 1056
folio_note: frame 1056: one typed block of 86 letters in 18 five-letter groups (the last of one letter), heading numbers 2318 1130 86 2865 (the third is the letter count); receipt stamp of the Fahrabteilung, "Eing. 24.11.33", journal no. 808/33
status: Typed exercise message, seen on the frame image (13 Nov 2026). No decipherment on the frame, read row by row at 0.8 of full size on 13 Nov 2026 and looked over at full size on 23 Nov 2026; its margins hold the registry's hand only (the document's number and day, the receipt stamp's entries, a folio number). The other frames of 1048-1100, apart from 1093 and 1094, were seen on a contact sheet at 0.04 of full size, and those of 1054-1058, 1092, 1095 and 1096 also in NARA's page text; none of them was read. Frame 1055, by NARA's page text the unit's draft cover letter of 30.11.33, sends its answer to an exercise message of 28.11.33, and by the maintainer's review it is filed as 808/33 too (the page text gives "808/73"). The filing links the two, but this message is of 18 Nov and was received on 24 Nov: that frame 1055 answers it is provisional, and the answer was not found. The letters are unevenly spread (index of coincidence 0.070 over 86 letters; evenly spread letters, such as the Enigma gives, come to about 0.038 at this length, give or take about 0.003), and the system is not identified. The groups as read on 13 Nov 2026 are in the README, with the doubtful letters marked. Class A rests on frame 1093, a sibling filed with its plain text below it, and is provisional: that plain text is aligned with only 94 of frame 1093's 112 letters, and no common system for the July and November messages is established. Not found on DECODE by four keyword searches. Not in the repository (known.py).
why: Reichswehr exercise traffic of 1933 in a system not yet identified, which no public source we found describes, with a possible sibling in the same file (frame 1093) whose plain text is written below it.
score_note: Scored from the frame images during the Nov 2026 NARA T405 sweep (research/sweep_2026-11-22_nara_t405/); viewed
verify: Look on roll 1 for the answer sent with frame 1055 and see whether it answers this message (frame 1055 names an exercise message of 28.11.33); compare the message number that frame 1055 cites (732/33 by NARA's page text) with frame 1056's own, which the reading of 13 Nov leaves partly unread; have a person read the handwritten notes on frame 1093; Bundesarchiv RH 57/72 (Geheimschriftwesen, 1934-35, with "ein Heft zu den Geheimschlüsseln im Reichsheer") may describe the system.

title: 3. Division, Berlin, 22 Jul 1933 → 3. (Preußische) Fahrabteilung, Berlin-Lankwitz: a Reichswehr exercise message ("Uebungsspruch") in five-letter groups
correspondents: 3. Division, Stonach (Berlin) → "Verteiler (Gruppe III)"; the copy received by the 3. (Preußische) Fahrabteilung, Berlin-Lankwitz
shelfmark: NARA RG 242, microfilm T405, roll 1 ("Number 1", NAID 332024052), frame 1094
folio_note: frame 1094: one typed block of 108 letters in 22 five-letter groups (the last of three letters), heading 2007 - 108 - 1515 - 7578 (the second number is the letter count); receipt stamp of the Fahrabteilung, "Eing. 25.7.33", journal no. 492/33
status: Typed exercise message, seen on the frame image (13 Nov 2026). No decipherment on the frame, read row by row at 0.8 of full size on 13 Nov 2026 and looked over at full size on 23 Nov 2026; its margins hold the registry's hand only (the document's number and day, the receipt stamp's entries, a folio number, the journal number). On frame 1093, under the Fahrabteilung's answer, a handwritten note headed "aufgenommen" may be its decipherment; as we read it, the note needs letters this message lacks and accounts for at most 68 of its 108 letters, so either it is not this text's plain text or our reading of it is wrong. No person has read the note, so it counts as unread here: this row holds only if the note is not this message's decipherment. The letters are unevenly spread (index of coincidence 0.072 over 108 letters; evenly spread letters, such as the Enigma gives, come to about 0.038 at this length, give or take about 0.003), and the system is not identified. The groups as read on 13 Nov 2026 are in the README, with the doubtful letters marked. Class A rests on frame 1093, the answer to this message, filed with a plain text below it, and is provisional: that plain text is aligned with only 94 of frame 1093's 112 letters, and no common system for the July and November messages is established. Not found on DECODE by four keyword searches. Not in the repository (known.py).
why: Reichswehr exercise traffic of 1933 in a system not yet identified, which no public source we found describes, with its answer on frame 1093 and that answer's plain text written below it.
score_note: Scored from the frame images during the Nov 2026 NARA T405 sweep (research/sweep_2026-11-22_nara_t405/); viewed
verify: Have a person read the two handwritten notes on frame 1093, first the one headed "aufgenommen": if it is this message's decipherment, this row is a read cipher, not a lead; test the system on the answer of frame 1093, whose plain text is written below it (single and double columnar transposition missed there under a sealed plan of 14 Nov 2026); Bundesarchiv RH 57/72 may describe the system.
